request.spec:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines
and every action in list order are unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines
and every action in list order are unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added a "Sort by" select (`data-testid="sort-by"`) to the people list, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

The only file changed is the front end, `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`:

- **Options:** added (the default), name, grade and due-total.
- **Name:** ignores case, the same way the app already compares names (so "ada" sorts before "Ben").
- **Grade:** uses each person's grade as of the sheet's today.
- **Due-total:** smallest first, using the capped figure the row shows, with n/a last.
- **Ties:** people with equal keys keep their list order.
- **Display only:** the sort only reorders the rows on screen. The stored positions, the rollup lines, the move up/down buttons and every other action that works in list order are unchanged.
- **Per user:** the sort belongs to each user's screen and stays in place when a sheet is loaded or re-loaded. Another user signed in elsewhere still sees the list in added order unless they pick a sort themselves.

No server or database changes were needed.
